key_insight: Neural approximation costs for semilinear parabolic PDE solution operators separate into governing-law complexity and data encoding, with a dimension-independent structural exponent that vanishes for polynomial nonlinearities.
engineering_relevance: The results motivate PDE-aware architectures with reusable nonlinear blocks and bounded learned weights per encoded mode, avoiding parameter growth tied directly to grid resolution or time-step refinement.
method: Parameterize the constitutive law as a single neural block using its computation-graph structure.
Encode input data separately and propagate pointwise block accuracy into stronger-norm bounds along the full trajectory.
Establish nearly matching upper and lower parameter bounds for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations with smooth Hamiltonians.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including O(log(1/η)) nonlinear-block cost for 2D Navier–Stokes and approximately η^(-1/s) parameters for C^s Hamiltonians, with a matching lower bound up to logarithms; no empirical evaluation is described.
watch_item: These are approximation guarantees for specified PDE classes, not guarantees of successful training or resolution-independent runtime.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
